AI post mortem
AI Post Mortem Promptcopy brief
Cursor✗
VERDICT: 0.14 for Desert Falcon was fair-to-slightly high in hindsight — the race went to a proven deep-ground horse at 28.0, not the short-priced form horses, so a ~14% win chance on another contender was reasonable but never looked like converting. Deep Havana lost because heavy Ayr exposed his profile: strong recent placing form (1-2222) and a firming market at 6.4 could not overcome draw 11 in a 25-runner 6f handicap, a 4lb higher mark than the winner (OR 95 vs 91, 9-12 vs 9-8), and no recorded finish in the places. Station X, drawn 5 with D 3-10 and a lighter weight, was the horse whose pre-race credentials matched the conditions; Deep Havana did not finish among the recorded places.
Missed We overweighted consistent recent seconds and market support on heavy ground where the winner’s deep-going record (D 3-10, dr5, lower weight) was the knowable edge.
Improve ground: in heavy Class 2 sprints, cap win probability for horses whose main edge is recent form on faster/mixed ground unless they have solid heavy/deep stats (not G 0-0 / thin D samples) before elevating them above proven deep-ground rivals.
Gemini✗
Deep Havana, despite being a strong board pick at 6.40 and the model's top selection, failed to feature in the placings of the Ladbrokes Ayr Silver Cup. The demanding heavy ground conditions likely played a significant role in its inability to contend, suggesting it couldn't produce its best form under such testing circumstances. It was comprehensively beaten by the 28.0 SP winner, Station X.
Missed We missed that Deep Havana was unable to translate its strong market and model backing into a competitive run on the heavy ground, and the winner emerged from a significantly longer price.
Improve ground: Verify Deep Havana's true suitability for heavy ground in future race planning, as this performance indicates a potential struggle in such conditions despite pre-race optimism.
NVIDIA✗
Deep Havana was fully committed and ridden to lead early, but the heavy ground and stiff six-furlong trip at Ayr proved too testing for the lightly raced six-year-old. Having never previously negotiated such a testing surface in a competitive handicap, he likely lacked the stamina and surefootedness to sustain his early challenge.
Missed The heavy ground and stiff trip were not factored into the 6.40 selection as primary liabilities.
Improve ground: validate footing tolerance before backing in heavy-ground handicaps
Lucy✗
Despite the recent form inconsistency of Deep Havana's yard, the horse was favored due to a decent odds ratio (OR) of 91 and a solid record in class 2 races. However, on the day, Station X, with longer odds, proved stronger, suggesting that Station X might have had better ground conditions or pace strategy which were not accounted for in our pre-race analysis.
Missed Pace
Improve pace: Consider assessing the likely race pace and positioning of horses at an earlier stage in the analysis.

Evening Saigon looks the most coherent win angle in a wide 25-runner Class 2. The Goodwood form is the anchor: he won a 27-runner handicap at this trip and grade last time, and before that was only 0.3L off in a deep Royal Ascot 6f, so the profile is of a horse competitive in big-field handicaps rather than a small-field flier. Soft suits on the figures (1-1 on going), he carries a useful 9-2 from OR 96 in a race where several rivals are more exposed or badly treated on trip, and draw 24 sits in the high third where Ayr’s six-furlong stats lean — useful rather than decisive at this field size, but it fits. I would not take Binhareer at 5.5 as automatic proof: Haggas/Marquand and 1-2 at Ayr are positives, yet he is only 1-4 on soft, draw 2 does not especially exploit the high bias, and the price reads more like stable/connections trust than clear soft-ground superiority.

The main risk is ground translation: his last win came on good to firm at Goodwood, and while the 1-1 soft record helps, it is a thin sample compared with proven mud merchants such as Fine Interview (5-9 on soft) or Ardisia (1-1 soft with 1-1 course-and-distance). official ratingspace map and possible pacemaker among Ryan’s pairAmir Lehbab’s recent work/fitness after 72 days
Amir Lehbab is the only runner with meaningful racecourse evidence at this level: a narrow second over seven furlongs in Class 2 at Doncaster on good ground, preceded by a close third at Newbury, from the card’s strongest trainer–jockey pairing in Andrew Balding and Oisin Murphy. In a nine-runner Class 2 with seven debutants, that proven competitiveness outweighs the blank soft-going and course-and-distance records; the others are essentially unraced guesses despite strong connections. Draw five sits in the middle third at Ayr seven furlongs, where high stalls have won most often historically, but that is a modest headwind rather than a reason to pass over the only horse with a form line.

The main danger is not the short price tag on the card but the combination of a seventy-two-day break and first-time soft ground, which leaves room for a well-prepared debutant — notably from Karl Burke or Edward Bethell — to outrun its market position. Kevin Ryan’s two runners look more like exposure runs after poor sole starts, so they are less of a direct threat than the fresh blood. I agree with the Going model’s default: Amir Lehbab remains the most logical winner on available evidence.

Cherry Cobbler is the most convincing profile on the evidence: 1-1 course and course-and-distance, including a July win here and a narrow Good-ground second over this exact 7f Class 4 trip in June (0.3L). That beats raw ratings or AW-heavy recent wins — Miletus won that June heat but has since finished fifth twice back at Newmarket, and Raggaas/Rogue Allegiance bring Crisford/Owen momentum without turf-Good or track proof. Cherry Cobbler’s mid draw (5) is a modest negative versus the high-stall 7f bias, but his repeated July form suggests he copes; top weight is earned rather than inflated.

The main risk is the handicap ceiling at 10-2 in a 15-runner 0-80, with several high-draw rivals (Leadman 14, Hardy's Hero 13, Hungarian 11) aligned to the 49% high-third draw trend and capable of outrunning patchy Good-ground records if the race sets up for hold-up closers. Leadman’s Ascot traffic excuse and class hike are real positives, but G 0-7 on Good keeps him behind the proven course form horse for the win slot.

He drops from Class 2 company into a weaker Class 4 field off a close second at Lingfield (beaten only 0.3L), and that run fits the model’s “strong speed for the grade” read; Epsom over 6f also shows he handles a stiff six rather than being purely a 5f type. Draw 3 is neutral in an eight-runner Chester field (low bias exists but is not dominant at this trip/size), and while soft is unproven on the card (0–0 on today’s going), his Epsom good-to-soft near-miss in hotter company is a reasonable proxy—unlike several rivals he is not trying to translate a single all-weather or good-ground-only figure onto Chester soft.

The biggest risk is ground and freshness: 78 days off, first-time headgear, and Pat Cosgrave’s recent post-mortem flag on good-ground disappointment—soft suitability is still the main unknown. Impulsive Spirit is the logical danger at 3.0 on top OR (82) and a debut win, but one Chepstow success is thin proof for Chester soft six and his draw 5 is only mid-tier here; Rhodes Runner gets a “saved-for-bigger” dampener on today’s lower prize and hung at Doncaster,…

Epictetus arrives with the clearest profile for this trip and grade: a Sandown win over 10f followed by a close Lingfield third shows he is fit, effective at this distance, and competitive in Class 4 company. He is not a short-price favourite, which I prefer here—Patagonia Girl’s Chester placings are useful but she has not converted them into wins over this trip, carries no soft-ground proof (G 0-0), and shares Hugo Palmer’s second string with an AW-only partner. Let’s Dream has the top OR and strong Chester CD figures, but the Southwell collapse and heavy 9-12 blunt that edge on today’s soft 10.5f.

The main risk to Epictetus is Chester itself: he is 0-0 at the course, the circuit’s camber and bends often flatter local specialists, and his last two wins came on good-to-firm rather than soft—though his broader going record (G 1-5) suggests he is not a non-stayer on slower ground. High draw (dr9) is a minor positive in the historical Chester 10f sample, but it is not decisive in an 11-runner field.

The sole AW 12f form line was not enough to overcome trip position, mark/weight, and a rival better treated by the handicapper and market.

Food For Thought is the most coherent win case on the card. The model’s prior is right to lean here: she shares top weight on 84, has the clearest upward profile (Nottingham win, two close seconds including Newmarket July over 10f on good-to-firm), and Beckett/Crouch is a solid combination even if the quoted 14-day blanks are stale. At 3.2 she is fairly priced rather than a steam ball, which fits a filly whose good-ground record is still thin (0-1 G) and who is stepping back from 10f with no course wins (C 0-0). Draw 3 is a negative at Newmarket 8f in a 9-runner field where high stalls win ~46% of winners, but that is not enough to overturn her on ability and recent form.

The biggest risk is suitability noise: today’s good ground and 8f are not fully proven, and low draw works against the historical course bias; if she does not translate the July form, Thaluna (draw 7, Haggas, 3rd in that July heat) or Stormy Music (proven 8f C&D winner but draw 1 and 6lb out of the weights) are the main alternatives. Prosperity’s 4.8 looks more market than turf proof (0-0 on good, AW/Ripon wins only), and Radiance is hard to fancy off yesterday’s Ayr flop despite the high draw.

A 0.30 win_prob was slightly too high in hindsight: it leaned on form and market favouritism while under-discounting the documented draw and good-8f gaps that mattered on the day.
Missed We under-weighted how much a low draw and unproven good 8f form would cap a 3.25 favourite on this specific Newmarket handicap layout.
Improve draw: apply a stronger stall-bias penalty for Newmarket 8f handicaps when the runner is drawn low (≤4) in fields of ~9, and require proven good-ground 8f form before assigning 30%+ win_prob.

His 2–6 on good ground and fresh 14-day reappearance put him ahead of the steamer **Gooloogong**, whose appeal rests more on market move and a single distance marker than on top-tier connections, and ahead of **Squire Danagher**, who is 0–6 on good and arrives off jumping PUs.

Nabati remains my pick, aligned with the Going baseline. Charlie Appleby’s yard is in exceptional nick (79% rtf), William Buick is the right rider for a tactical 6f Class 1, and the profile fits this test: 6f winner on good ground, fresh off an authoritative Newmarket win, and a 3-1-2-1 pattern that reads as progressive rather than one-note. Draw 5 is neutral in this eight-runner field where high stalls have a modest edge, and I am not elevating Arapaho Gold simply because he is shortest in the market — three wins are positive, but the step from his Newbury novice success into this company, plus 9st 6lb and a low draw in a race where winners skew high, keeps him behind Nabati on suitability rather than price.

The main risk is that Nabati’s listed form is still built around a Class 4 win; Jolivette is the most credible alternative, having already run close in genuine Class 1 6f fields (0.8L fifth at Newmarket July, 0.5L ninth in a deep Ascot handicap) from draw 8 where the course draw stats lean, with Andrew Balding’s stable ranking #2 nationally. Arapaho Gold’s unbeaten record and 1-1 at Newbury demand respect as the market leader, but without proven Good-ground or six-furlong…

post-win OR reassessment after two dominant Newmarket winsearly pace map and whether Castle Rock gets a lead or must rally widedraw effect calibrated specifically for 20 runners on Newbury 7f
Castle Rock is the logical anchor: the Going baseline aligns with the form. He is 2/2 on Good (including a 7f win) and arrives off back-to-back Newmarket wins under Charlie Appleby and William Buick, a combo the model rightly flags and that fits a lightly raced but clearly progressive profile. Draw 10 is neutral-to-fine in a 20-runner field (mid third), and while the Newbury fourth on softer ground and a 42-day gap are minor dampeners, nothing in the runner list screams a definitive reason to demote him below horses with patchier profiles or worse draw slots on this track.

The biggest risk is the class-and-experience leap — only three career starts, stepping into a deep 0–95 Class 3 with 20 runners where analogs here have thrown up plenty of double-figure winners. The Fingal Raven is the main alternative: third at Goodwood over this trip in a similar C3 handicap (beaten 0.8L) with Jamie Osborne’s yard in strong form (70% rtf), and he looks the most likely to capitalise if Castle Rock finds this mark too hot. Startled’s 7f Good form and kinder OR are appealing at 7.6, but Richard Hughes’s yard strike rate tempers enthusiasm.

AI Post Mortem Promptcopy brief
Cursor✗
Tawaazon lost because the race was taken by low-draw Invincible Crown (dr2) on a 5f AW sprint where the missing early-pace map mattered: wide dr9 gave no positional edge and the winner's dr2 profile fits a handy trip. Tawaazon's own case was weak on this test — CD 0-0, D 1-10, recent 554959 and LR21 — so he was outrun rather than unlucky on ability alone. VERDICT: 0.26 for Ellie's de Vega was too high in hindsight; neither Kirby runner won and the card went to a 14.0 dr2 outsider, not the 3.8 market leader we weighted.
Missed Low draws controlled the early pace and the winner came from dr2, exactly the AW 5f scenario flagged but not verified pre-race.
Improve pace: map Newcastle 5f AW fields for early speed by draw before siding with wide-draw favorites or same-yard leaders.
NVIDIA✗
Tawaazon was well-backed at 3.50 with a stated win probability of 0.38, but finished well clear of the frame behind a 14.0 SP winner. The horse lacked the early speed to bridge the pace gap and was left chasing the pace throughout the 5f trip. The 14.0 SP winner travelled strongly and proved too free of traffic to reel in.
Missed Tawaazon unable to overcome a moderate draw and lacked the early dash to find a forward position in a straight 5f handicap.
Improve draw: Tawaazon needed a more favourable stalls draw to secure a handy position and avoid being held up in the early stages.
Lucy✗
Tawaazon struggled in this race, possibly due to the higher class (OR 54) and unfavorable market odds (14.0), which may have affected his motivation. His form on all-weather tracks has been inconsistent with a 0-1 record at this distance and course.
Missed We underestimated the impact of class and market on Tawaazon's performance.
Improve form: Focus on finding a more promising race for Tawaazon, considering his current form and the higher class he competed in this time.

CursorKnocknagoran Lady · 13%
Risk Unproven at Navan and only 1-6 on Good in a large field where one jumping error ends the chance.
Navan course formofficial race classlikely pace and whether she needs to lead or can stalk
Knocknagoran Lady is the most convincing profile in a messy 19-runner handicap. She arrives off a big-field win at Down Royal (1/22) only 22 days ago, with earlier proof she stays this far and acts on Good — notably the Kilbeggan 25f success and a close fourth over 24f at Roscommon. At 11-11 with a claim she is not top weight, the trip fits, and her recent jumping has been completion-first rather than punctuated by P/F/U like several market rivals. Can Happen steams despite a Galway pull-up, Magic Day is a perennial placer without a Good-ground win, and the saved-for-bigger profiles (Sammy Smart, Midleton Rare, Toor Khov) are structural dampeners rather than win angles in a low-prize heat.

The main risk is that this is still a wide-open handicap with sparse Navan form across the field: her Down Royal win came with limited detail on trip/going, she is only 1-6 on Good, and a 19-runner hurdle can turn on one mistake or a poor pace setup — she is a reasoned favourite, not a short-priced certainty.

CursorRocky Alfonso · 14%
Risk Good-ground suitability unproven vs his yielding-soft run, with top-yard debutants capable of leapfrogging modest exposed form.
official ratings once assignedearly pace and run-style map in a 15-runner maidenmeaningful draw positions if stalls are used
Among fifteen mostly unraced four-year-olds over 16f on good ground, the clearest evidence sits with the small group that have already run. Rocky Alfonso’s Roscommon fourth, beaten only half a length over sixteen furlongs, is the strongest raw figure in the field; S Curling’s yard is lower profile than the big stables but has a horse that has already shown stamina and competitiveness at this trip. Sharbel offers the nearest direct analogue—Galway sixteen furlongs on good, beaten 1.5L—with Derek O’Connor, who won over this course and trip on good ground on Timurshah, but the 150.0 quote suggests the market expects little improvement. Ellen Imlach is the meaningful market leader at 5.7 on Gordon Elliott/H C Swan debut credentials and a useful filly weight concession, yet with no exposed form and a modest €6,479 prize that invites the “saved for bigger” dampener on a top yard, I would not treat that price as proof of superiority over Rocky Alfonso’s tangible run.
